anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.text:
gauntlet: question

## Today
Every caller reads its settings through one shared resolver, and the timeout override is not reaching the caller that needs it.

## The change
The request adds a second settings file so that caller can get its timeout override.

## What I checked
- Held: Every caller reads settings through the same resolver.
- Corrected: The draft says the resolver cannot accept overrides; it already accepts a timeout override, so the missing override can be passed through the resolver without a second settings file.

A second settings file would duplicate the existing settings path and leave the real gap in place: the caller does not pass its override to the resolver. Which outcome should we pursue?
A) as framed: add the second settings file for the timeout override
B) pivot: have the caller pass its timeout override through the existing resolver - it already supports overrides, so this fixes the actual cause
C) smaller or none: document the default timeout and ship no override; the caller keeps the default
Recommendation: B - the resolver already handles overrides, so fixing the caller closes the gap without adding a parallel settings path.
